cover_subtitle: How I fixed a broken reply in 3 hours

slides.title: Step 1 – Read & Tag
slides.body: → Set Claude to read new emails. → Use simple regex (e.g., “Subject:”) to extract the topic. → Store the tag in a JSON file.

slides.title: Step 2 – Prompt for Draft
slides.body: → Prompt Claude: “Write a reply for a [tag] email.” → Include placeholders for subject and sender. → Test with a sample email.

slides.title: Step 3 – Debug the Prompt
slides.body: → My first prompt omitted the subject placeholder. → Claude returned a generic thank‑you. → Add “subject” token, retest.

slides.title: Step 4 – Stripe Test
slides.body: → Insert test secret key from Stripe dashboard. → Ensure no extra spaces or line breaks. → Run a $1 test charge.

slides.title: Step 5 – End‑to‑End Check
slides.body: → Send a real inquiry email. → Verify tag, draft, and reply are all correct. → Confirm Stripe webhook fires and records payment.
